newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan assembly approves peace accord.
newsitem.headline: Sudan assembly approves peace accord.

text.p: Sudan's parliament on Wednesday approved a peace accord the government signed with former rebel factions which aims to end the war in southern Sudan.
State radio said the National Assembly unanimously passed a constitutional decree which embodies the peace accord between the Islamist government and six southern factions.
The decree must still be signed by Sudan's President Lieutenant-General Omar Hassan al-Bashir to become law.
The accord does not include the main southern rebel group Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA), led by John Garang.

Parliament's approval includes endorsement of interim arrangements in southern Sudan. The agreement signed in April says there will be a four-year transitional period during which southern Sudanese are meant to decide whether to secede.
Two privately owned newspapers quoted Bashir on Wednesday as saying that the objective of the accord was to stop the 14-year-old war and usher in a period of development.
He said his government was determined to ensure that the referendum was free and fair.
"The government will abide by the results of the referendum if it leads to separation of the south from the north," he was quoted as saying by al-Rai al-Akher newspaper.
"I would like us to concentrate in the present period on convincing the southern brothers of the unity of Sudan," Akhbar al-Youm quoted Bashir as saying.
The assembly added amendments to the decree which entail appointing governors in 10 south Sudan states, the radio said.
A parliament source said Bashir would appoint a coordinating council president to suggest candidates for governors.
